spec.question: Can Microseed construct a non-executable multi-step epistemic program from organism-owned opaque learned structure without caller-supplied sequence identity, while preserving exact authority/currentness boundaries?
spec.incumbent: Existing learned-relation, opaque-projection, program-construction, qualification and currentness owners are sufficient to construct a candidate program as a non-executable object.
spec.rival: Apparent endogenous program construction depends on caller/fixture leakage of sequence identity or semantic action labels.
spec.manipulation: Build matched fixtures with identical learned action/outcome relational structure and qualified primitive capabilities, but independently permute opaque primitive IDs and the hidden successful sequence; remove all caller-supplied sequence/semantic names before candidate construction.
controls: execution permission withheld in every research condition
stale one primitive capability epoch after candidate construction
spec.incumbent_prediction: The same relationally implied program structure is reconstructed under opaque-ID permutations, remains non-executable without separate authorization, and stales when a bound primitive dependency stales.
spec.rival_prediction: Construction collapses to chance, changes with surface labels, or requires the oracle/caller sequence; alternatively the candidate remains executable/current after permission/dependency removal.
spec.measurement: Exact candidate program step structure modulo opaque-ID permutation; provenance/dependency bindings; authorization bit/ability to invoke; stale/current state after primitive epoch drift.
spec.minimal_embodiment: Research-only fixture/test around existing endogenous-program and bound-request owners; no production code changes. Reuse existing program/history constructors where possible.
spec.falsifier: Failure to reconstruct under opaque permutation without oracle sequence, or any execution authority acquired solely by candidate construction.
spec.loop_plus: If construction fails, distinguish missing representation/program owner from search-budget or evidence-access failure before proposing mechanism.
